items.t: 디딤, 'AI-Cloud Big Tech 2026'에서 AI 데이터센터(AIDC) 운영 혁신 전략 발표
items.d: AX·DX 전문기업 디딤(대표 장민호)이 10월 1일 양재 엘타워에서 열린 'AI-Cloud Big Tech 2026'에 참석하여 AI 데이터센터(AIDC) 운영 및 관제 전략에 대한 세션 발표를 성공적으로 마쳤다고 밝혔다. 과학기술정보통신부가 후원하고 한국인공지능클라우드산업협회(KACI)가 주최한 'AI-Cloud Big Tech 2026'은 Agentic AI의 발전, AI·클라우드 기업 간의 연결, 산업 현장의 전환을 모색하기 위해 마련된
items.fullText: 경제 중기·벤처 디딤, 'AI-Cloud Big Tech 2026'에서 AI 데이터센터(AIDC) 운영 혁신 전략 발표 발행일 : 2026-10-02 10:13 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 이영수 디딤 부사장이 세션 발표를 진행하고 있다. 사진=디딤 AX·DX 전문기업 디딤(대표 장민호)이 10월 1일 양재 엘타워에서 열린 'AI-Cloud Big Tech 2026'에 참석하여 AI 데이터센터(AIDC) 운영 및 관제 전략에 대한 세션 발표를 성공적으로 마쳤다고 밝혔다. 과학기술정보통신부가 후원하고 한국인공지능클라우드산업협회(KACI)가 주최한 'AI-Cloud Big Tech 2026'은 Agentic AI의 발전, AI·클라우드 기업 간의 연결, 산업 현장의 전환을 모색하기 위해 마련된 대표 전문 행사로 국내외 관련 업계 종사자들이 참석한 가운데 다양한 기업 기술 강연과 전시 부스가 운영되었다. 이날 디딤은 3부 기업 기술 강연 세션에서 'Revolution of AIDC, AI 데이터센터가 바꾸는 인프라 산업의 판도, 그리고 운영의 시대'를 주제로 발표를 진행했다. 발표자로 나선 디딤 CAO 이영수 부사장은 급격히 확산되는 AI 데이터센터 트렌드와 함께, 인프라 패러다임이 단순 '건설 및 구축'에서 '지속 가능한 운영 및 관제'의 영역으로 이동하고 있음을 강조했다. 이 부사장은 “AIDC는 기존 IDC 대비 랙당 전력 밀도가 수배 이상 높고 액랭식 냉각이 필수적인 만큼, 설비의 가동 중단을 방지하고 유효 연산 처리량을 극대화하는 운영 품질이 핵심 경쟁력”이라며, “디딤은 현재 국내 최대급 규모인 약 1만 장의 하이엔드 GPU 인프라를 직접 관제·운영하며 독보적인 현장 레퍼런스를 쌓아가고 있다”고 밝혔다. 특히 디딤은 이번 발표를 통해 애플리케이션 프로세스부터 물리 자원, 전력 및 냉각 설비까지 단일 모델로 통합 관리하는 'Full-Stack 가시성' 체계와 497종에 달하는 초밀도 메트릭 관측 카탈로그를 소개해 참석자들의 큰 호응을 얻었다. 이와 함께 현장 운용 경험이 결집된 통합 관제 솔루션인 'DidimOpSuite'를 선보이며, 수치 기반의 투명한 운영 성과 입증 방안을 함께 제안했다. 이영수 디딤 부사장은 “이번 행사 발표를 통해 AI 데이터센터 운영 분야에서 디딤이 가진 독보적인 기술력과 실전 경험을 업계에 명확히 알릴 수 있었다”라며, “앞으로도 AI 인프라의 안정적인 가동을 지원하는 최적의 파트너로서 국내 AI-Cloud 생태계 전환과 확산을 선도해 나갈 것”이라고 전했다. 이원지 기자 news21g@etnews.com

items.t: Lyft is paying $272.5M to settle lawsuit over how it classified drivers
items.d: Today, gig economy drivers are classified as contractors. This settlement clears up a lingering lawsuit from 2020 when that was still an unanswered issue.
items.fullText: Lyft has agreed to pay $272.5 million to settle a lawsuit accusing the ride-hailing company of violating California law by misclassifying drivers as independent contractors, instead of employees. The company said in a regulatory filing that it believes the settlement will allow it to avoid the “costs and distraction of protracted litigation and enable management to maintain its focus on executing its business objectives.” The settlement stems from a lawsuit filed by the California Labor Commissioner’s Office in August 2020 that accused Lyft of treating drivers as independent contractors rather than as employees, as required under state law at the time. The lawsuit alleged that drivers were denied minimum wage and overtime, as well as other benefits and protections provided to employees, including paid sick leave and timely wage payments. “This settlement is about the workers who came forward and spoke up. Their voices made this outcome possible,” California Labor Commissioner Lilia García-Brower said in a statement , adding that the LCO will forgo its share of the settlement and direct those funds to drivers who filed wage claims. The settlement, which still must be approved by a judge, covers alleged violations from April 6, 2016, to December 15, 2020 — a period California was grappling with whether workers in the booming gig economy were independent contractors or employees. Today, drivers for app-based transportation services like Lyft and Uber are classified as contractors after voters passed ballot measure Proposition 22 in 2020. The ballot measure provided a carve-out from Assembly Bill 5 , a state law passed in 2019 that required companies like DoorDash, Lyft, and Uber to classify gig workers as employees, entitling them to minimum wage, workers’ compensation, and other benefits. September 30, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Building on nearly a decade of co-engineering, CoreWeave has built NVIDIA compute, networking and software into a cloud purpose-built for AI that’s still returning on investment across multiple generations of deployment. Now, CoreWeave is bringing the next generation of NVIDIA infrastructure to production. At CoreWeave Fully Connected, running this week in San Francisco, CoreWeave announced availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems with Spectrum-X 102.4T Ethernet networking. Cognition, the applied AI lab behind the Devin AI software engineer, is the first customer running production workloads on Vera Rubin. CoreWeave will also offer NVIDIA Vera , the first CPU built for AI agents. In addition, CoreWeave launched CoreWeave Forge, a connected environment for training, evaluating and improving models and agents on NVIDIA accelerated computing. “NVIDIA accelerated computing delivers value across generations,” said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “CoreWeave’s NVIDIA V100 GPUs are still running customer workloads nearly a decade after Volta launched, even as CoreWeave brings Vera Rubin NVL72 into production. items.fullText: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack Open research, controls across the agent stack and continuous testing help defenders build and operate more secure AI systems. September 21, 2026 by Saša Zdjelar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI security is an engineering problem. That means defined security requirements, enforceable controls, named owners and evidence that protections work. As AI becomes more capable, the industry must accelerate security engineering, broaden access to defensive tools and share what works faster. Technology Changes, Security Fundamentals Endure The internet and cloud computing changed how software operates, while core security responsibilities endured: establish identity, control access, limit exposure and verify that protections work. AI agents introduce new capabilities — reasoning , using tools and adapting actions based on the data they encounter. Those capabilities require applying established principles to new operating conditions. This pace creates pressure. Organizations want the productivity benefits of AI while the practices to govern and secure these systems are still developing. Security Depends on the Full Agent Stack Applications depend on code, data, identities, services and infrastructure. Security depends on how those components work together — and AI agents extend that system . Models provide capabilities; harnesses organize context, tools and workflows; and runtime environments provide the infrastructure within which actions execute. Each part of that stack carries security responsibilities, and proper protection requires controls across each layer, as data, instructions and actions move through the system. A new creature-catching adventure is ready to stream from the cloud this week. Pawprint Studio’s Aniimo arrives on GeForce NOW at launch, inviting gamers to explore the vibrant continent of Idyll across supported devices. Also this week, 007 First Light receives a path-tracing update on GeForce NOW, alongside a smashing limited-time Deluxe Edition sale on Steam and Epic Games Store . Gaijin Network’s fractured-multiverse action game Active Matter and Annapurna Interactive’s acclaimed space mystery Outer Wilds are also among 11 new titles joining the cloud this week. Explore Idyll With the Cutest Companions The path to Idyll begins now. Aniimo is a free-to-play, open-world creature-catching role-playing game where every creature encountered can become a companion. Catch Aniimo with Aniipods, then Twine with them to take on their form and use unique skills to solve puzzles, win battles and overcome challenges. Glide, dive and burrow across Idyll, then return to a personal RV to build a warm, interactive Homeland alongside Aniimo companions. Stream Aniimo on a Steam Deck , in the newly supported Firefox browser and across any other supported devices — without waiting through its 45GB download or making room in local storage.
